bullets.title: A fan-engaged option for the podcast
bullets.note:
From June – Dec., 2019, I’m removing ads and sponsors from the podcast for a six-month experiment. It’s a big deal for me and might end sooner if it doesn’t work at all.

The podcast will continue to be 100% free for everyone. Then, there is a new upgraded option: for people who would like to [contribute a few dollars (or more) per month](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/68u8wxgppu8hpz20q/8efqhoh2pr4vp8/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy9zdXBwb3J0Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWNvbnZlcnRraXQmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1jb252ZXJ0a2l0JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj01YmY=) to support the podcast and everything else I do, **I will offer a live video Q&A each month... just for this much smaller group of supporters. bullets.section: Shelter I’ve been testing in the wilderness —
bullets.title: SHIFTPOD2
bullets.note: I first saw a SHIFTPOD at Burning Man, where the 60-second set-up blew me away (here’s a [video example of a first-time set-up](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/68u8wxgppu8hpz20q/52hvh7hno6e8zz/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj0zMXNXdndMTmJ0dw==)). The reflective material allows you to sleep comfortably in hot environments, and while too heavy for backpacking (best guess is 60 pounds), it’s perfect for packing into the desert or wilderness via car or horse. It comfortably sleeps 4-6 people. I’ve been testing the SHIFTPOD2 in forest environments, and it’s been fantastic thus far. Here’s a description ([source](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/68u8wxgppu8hpz20q/qxu8h7h42kx506/aHR0cHM6Ly9kcml2ZW54ZGVzaWduLmNvbS9ub3cvcHJvamVjdC5hc3A_SUQ9MTY0NTI=)): “Shiftpods are the best heavy-duty, pop-up shelter system on this planet — great for festivals, camping, overlanding, refugee camps…. The redesigned range brings more headroom, black out flies, door screens, military grade Kevlar stitching, and a new double sealed seam system for the best weather protection available. Deployed all over the world, the Shiftpod has proven itself as a lightweight, heavy-duty, reliable shelter in the worst conditions imaginable. From disaster shelters to festival living, the Shiftpod has you covered.” You can [read a review here](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/68u8wxgppu8hpz20q/9zizhnh6357mlg/aHR0cHM6Ly9mZXN0aXZhbHNxdWFkLmNvbS8yMDE2LzA1L3Byb3MtY29ucy1zaGlmdHBvZHMv), and you might also need to [watch the following video](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/68u8wxgppu8hpz20q/nlfohvhx57dpk3/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj05N24tQ0VBOXVlRQ==) on how to use the tie-downs, which I didn’t need in low-wind conditions. My only criticism is that I didn’t find an instruction manual in my shipment, and I was already in the woods, so I had to wing it. That also tells you how intuitive most of it is, except for the “blast shield,” which I couldn’t get on by myself.
